# Figentra Flow

Spec-driven development for agent teams: specs, approval stops, tasks, the gate, landing and releases.

## What it is

Figentra Flow (`fflow`) is spec-driven development for agent teams. A change starts as a spec, stops for a human's
approval, becomes a plan and tasks, passes a gate and lands as a reviewed pull request. Flow keeps each spec, plan,
task and test in step, and refuses to move on when they drift.

- **Specs and approval stops:** `/flow-specify`, `/flow-clarify` and `/flow-plan` for Claude Code, OpenCode, Codex and
  other agents, with the templates and checks behind them.
- **One command for a repository's agent setup:** `fflow sync` renders the commands, skills, agents, rules, guard
  hooks, git hooks and CI workflows from a preset, and `fflow check` fails CI when any of them drifts.
- **The gate and landing:** `fflow gate run` runs your checks at the pushed head, and `fflow land` merges only a
  green, approved pull request. Release trains and releases follow the same rules.
- **Adapters:** the tracker (Linear or GitHub Issues), the runner (GitHub Actions or your own box), credentials and
  secrets are chosen per repository.

- **Task context:** `fflow context` finds scoped instructions, packages, skills and guidance in one checkout or the
  registered collection, with revisions and dirty state. See the [context guide](packages/flow/README.md#task-context-and-documentation-boundaries).

A preset carries a team's conventions: Flow ships `neutral` for any repository and `stackra` for Stackra's own.

## Architecture

One pnpm workspace with one package, `packages/flow`: plain ESM JavaScript with JSDoc. Its runtime
dependencies are `undici` and the console engine (`@stackra/console`, `@stackra/validation`), which only the CLI layer
loads.

| Path                         | What                                                                         |
| ---------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/flow/bin`          | the `fflow` dispatcher                                                       |
| `packages/flow/src/commands` | one module per command (`init`, `sync`, `gate`, `land`, `train`, `release`…) |
| `packages/flow/src/adapters` | the tracker and runner adapters                                              |
| `packages/flow/assets/flow`  | the `neutral` and `stackra` presets and the base templates                   |
| `packages/flow/schema`       | the `flow.config.json` schema                                                |

## This repository

# Figentra Flow: agent guide

One pnpm workspace, one package: `packages/flow` (`@figentra-oss/flow`, binaries `fflow` and deprecated `figentra-flow`). The manifest and
`.github/workflows/release.yml` describe publication; a checkout version alone is not release evidence.

| Path                          | What                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                             |
| ----------------------------- | ---------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `packages/flow/bin/fflow.mjs` | the dispatcher: `fflow <command>` runs `src/commands/<command>.mjs`'s `run(args)`                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                |
| `packages/flow/src/commands`  | `init`, `sync`, `migrate`, `spec`, `gate`, `trace`, `parse`, `linear`, `start`, `clean`, `guard`, `land`, `train`, `team`, `status`, `mcp`, plus `gate-run` (the `run` mode of `gate`); each exports `run(args)` → exit code                                                                                                                                                                                     |
| `packages/flow/src/lib`       | `spec-parse` (pure parsers), `linear` and `net` (the Linear client), `git` and `workspace` (worktrees), `gate-post` (the box poster, copied into each gate job), `github` (`gh api` through `bot:gh`), `owner-only`, `required-checks`, `approve-check` and `approve-workflow` (the owner-only list, trusted required checks, the approval check the workflow runs from the package, and the workflow, STA-1856) |
| `packages/flow/assets`        | `flow/presets/{neutral,stackra}` (templates, the ten `flow-*` commands, the steward `agents/`, the `rules/` (the worktree rule, STA-1871), and `preset.yml`'s approval secret names; stackra also carries core's role agents, rules, `skills/`, `reference/`, `routing.yaml` and `models.yaml`, STA-1945), `flow/templates` (checklist, constitution); spec-kit-derived files carry `derived-from` (ADR 0510)    |

## Rules

- Commands run in the repository they act on: `ROOT` is the working directory.
- Plain ESM JavaScript with JSDoc; runtime dependencies are `undici`, `@stackra/console` and `@stackra/validation`; `tsc` checks it (`checkJs`) and emits the declarations.
- Tests are `node:test` files in `src/__tests__/`, next to their subjects; no network, no real Linear call.
- `assets/flow/` is Flow's own: change a preset's template or command there; `fflow sync` renders it, and the `derived-from` line stays until a file is rewritten from scratch (ADR 0510).
- Secrets: `fflow linear` reads `LINEAR_AGENT_TOKEN` or `LINEAR_API_KEY` from the environment, which the calling
  caller provides (core's `secrets-exec.mjs --names …`, or a CI job's sops decrypt step). Never read, print or
  commit a token.
- Worktrees live only in `.claude/worktrees/` (Stackra ADR 0503): make one with `fflow start`, remove one with
  `fflow clean`. Worktree tests use the local repository fixture in `src/__tests__/__fixtures__/`.
- Done = CI green after the merge, its `test` job included ("Tests run later" below). Conventional commits; a changeset for every package change.

## Tests run later: merge now, label `needs-testing`

Owner decision 2026-11-03 (STA-2083, replaces "Tests run on the box"): nothing waits on tests before it lands. No box
run before the merge and no waiting on CI: open the pull request and merge it right away
(`gh pr merge --squash --admin`), then add the Linear label `needs-testing` to its STA issue and a
`Needs testing: <what to run>` line to the pull request body. The tester lane later runs those tests on the box
(`testbed run "FLOW STA-n" . "pnpm verify"`) and removes the label. Since 2026-11-04 (owner default O4) CI's
`test` job runs the package's tests on every pull request and push to main; it is not a required check, so a red
`test` never blocks a merge, but it is fixed before the work counts as done. Nothing installs or tests on a
workstation.

## Task navigation

Use `fflow context --path packages/flow --json` for bounded navigation, or repository search before Flow
is installed. Read [the package context guide](packages/flow/README.md#task-context-and-documentation-boundaries)
for owners, examples, verification and standalone/collection behavior. Change preset guidance in
`assets/flow/presets/*/surfaces/agents-md/agents.md`, not consumers' rendered instructions. Codex already uses the
harness in `src/adapters/harness/index.mjs`; do not add a duplicate adapter. These paths are relative to the package.

## How work flows

Every change goes through Figentra Flow (`fflow`, the stackra preset). Specs live in `.agents/specs/`.

- Every branch and pull request carries a linear key (`STA-<n>`); branches are
  `figentra/<key>-<slug>`.
- Spec the change with `/flow-specify`, `/flow-clarify` and `/flow-plan` (it writes the tasks too), then build it
  with `/flow-implement`.
- Work in a worktree under `.claude/worktrees/<name>/`, made with `fflow start <key>`; never next to the repository.
- Land with `fflow land <pr>`: it waits for the gate and removes the worktree after the merge.

## Rules

- Commits are Conventional Commits with a `Refs: <key>` line. Never `--no-verify`, never `LEFTHOOK=0`.
- Secrets are named, never written: no value in a file, a commit, a log or a message.
- The git hooks run the mise-pinned oxfmt and oxlint (`mise exec npm:oxfmt -- oxfmt <files>`), so a commit needs no
  install; where mise is missing they are skipped and CI checks.
- This file, `CLAUDE.md`, `lefthook.yml`, `.mcp.yaml` and the agent setup are rendered by `fflow sync`. Do not edit
  them: change `.flow/overrides/` or `flow.config.json`, run `fflow sync`, and `fflow check` shows any drift.

## Rules index

Each rule is one file. Read the ones that fit the task before editing; not every client loads them on its own.

- `.claude/rules/ai-tools.md`: Every AI tool, server or client, is generated from its own module's declarations; nobody writes or registers a tool by hand (always)
- `.claude/rules/concurrent-sessions.md`: Managing multiple concurrent AI agent sessions (always)
- `.claude/rules/http-conventions.md`: HTTP API conventions for Stackra services (authored as action and query classes; endpoints derived by convention; Encore is generated) (always)
- `.claude/rules/linear.md`: Work is not done until its Linear issue is in the right state; agents use `pnpm linear` (always)
- `.claude/rules/module-boundary.md`: Module boundary and import rules for Stackra (always)
- `.claude/rules/naming-and-casing.md`: One naming convention for Stackra. Files kebab-case with a kind suffix, class names from the file, identities derived, machine codes snake_case, namespace lookups with ::, env and secrets SCREAMING_SNAKE. (always)
- `.claude/rules/not-built-yet.md`: Technologies rejected or deferred. Do not introduce them helpfully; route to the owner. (always)
- `.claude/rules/secrets.md`: Secret management and environment configuration (always)
- `.claude/rules/service-checklist.md`: The eight things a complete service has before it is done. (for `services/**`)
- `.claude/rules/task-vocabulary.md`: The fixed set of package.json script names every member uses, and the root commands that fan them out. (for `**/package.json`, `turbo.jsonc`)
- `.claude/rules/tenancy.md`: Two-layer tenant isolation rules, plus the scope-tree rules (free code; depth by plan). Read when adding the first tenant-owned table or touching tenant-scoped code; not loaded by default.
- `.claude/rules/third-party-sources.md`: What an agent may read, port or copy from another project, and what must travel with ported code. (for `apps/**`, `packages/**`, `services/**`, `workers/**`, `tools/**`)
- `.claude/rules/versions.md`: Version pinning and catalog rules for Stackra monorepo (always)
- `.claude/rules/workspace-layout.md`: Repository directory structure and placement rules (always)
- `.claude/rules/worktrees.md`: One worktree per active task under .claude/worktrees/, removed when the work ends, never at the cost of work or outputs (always)

## Find the task's context

- Start with `fflow context --path <repository-relative-path> --json` (or repository search when Flow is unavailable).
  Read README and applicable ancestor/member AGENTS instructions, including overrides, before editing. Read the
  rules the index above names for the paths you touch.
- Locate the owning package/service, its current contract and decisions, implementation, example and tests. Follow
  exports, callers, fixtures and generator sources for shared changes. An index is navigation, not verification.
- For collection work use `fflow context --all --query <phrase>`; each checkout keeps its own revision and authority.
  A standalone clone must use its pinned framework/preset guidance, not require a sibling checkout or private notes.
- Read a skill's `SKILL.md` only when its trigger fits; check prerequisites and version compatibility before following it.
- Keep README at meaningful package, service or component-family boundaries. Explain purpose, public entry points,
  a working example and allowed verification. Keep component contracts in types and examples; do not add one README
  or AGENTS file per component, function or ordinary folder. Preserve existing mandatory member guidance.
- Keep cross-cutting capabilities in the existing catalogue/guide: owner of each step, contracts, consumers, relevant
  authorization/failure boundaries and tests. Keep decisions in ADRs, procedures in skills and operational steps in runbooks.
- Distinguish accepted decisions, checkout implementation, passing checks at a revision, releases and deployments.
  Report missing evidence and conflicting sources. Verify only in the environment the repository permits.
